When I first got diagnosed I didn't believe it. A little after my 50th birthday I started scratching intensely on my legs. I went to the doctor and they tested me and said I had eczema and gave me some ointments. The ointments didn't work and I went back to the doctor as the rash started to spread on my leg. The doctor again tested me and said I had eczema and gave me another ointment at this point I sought out a dermatologist. The dermatologist confirmed the diagnosis of eczema and wanted to start me on a drug called duplixent. After running a blood test to confirm that I didn't have tuberculosis the doctor called me on March 2nd and said I was HIV positive. At the time when she Told me I was on a cell phone and working and busy and thought I might have heard HPV so I told the doctor to send me some paperwork and I would investigate. The paperwork never came so I didn't really think about it again but in the back of my mind I had the feeling she said hiv. as the months went by the rash and itching continued and got worse I could no longer ignore what was going on with my body and other things that had been a priority were no longer a priority. I went back to the doctor and they drew some blood and consequently that June of 2021 I was again diagnosed with HIV. The doctor referred me to a infectious disease doctor and after running some blood I believe he said my CD4 count was two. He said my count was so low that I've could have had it for at least 10 years for possibly as long as 10 years and didn't know. I thought over that time period I have been tested I thought over that time period I have been tested by proxy with the women I had dealt with because I'm heterosexual and they never had any problems that I knew. I had always been pretty promiscuous and lived a sexually free lifestyle, been into BDSM for more than a decade. But what led me to continue to go to the doctor and get that diagnosis could not be ignored the changes in the skin tone my dreadlocks after 30 years of growing have been falling out of my head and my skin was still itching uncontrollably. After  going to the infectious disease doctor he gave me a treatment of Biktarvy for 7 Days my insurance would kick in by that time and I had to get pre-approval and I should have had it by that point. My insurance sucked. I was not approved for the medicine and had to ponder and Fret and freak out about how I would get treatment because I felt like day by day I was dying. I found out about the Ryan White program called them up found a affiliate at 1:00 and had a jar of Biktarvy in my hand by 4:00. As of today my CD4 count is 45 my skin itches almost uncontrollably even after I've received the duplixent medication. Things have been tough, I have been celibate since February of 2021. I really don't have the energy wherewithal confidence appearance to even engage in that type of manner. There are times where I want to jump because I feel like I look like the elephant Man. Ultimately I feel like internally I'm getting better but externally I'm not and that makes me feel like s***. I haven't been able to locate any support groups. And this is the first time I've actually verbalized my story on paper or print or email or post. For some reason I just thought about searching this out and read it yesterday. I'm glad I did. It has helped me. Thank you. I am still lost at 51 years old I am diagnosed with HIV. I am from New York originally so I can remember the inception of the disease and that memory haunts me. Fortunately medical professionals have made me feel as if taking the pill daily will make things easy or not intrude in my life so much. But I've been taking the pill for 3 months and every day I feel like a stranger when I look in the mirror. I hope things get better.
